machinery: src/opentallas/critical_path.py (priced by roofline.serial_step on every study point)

serial_latency_inputs.purpose: Inputs of the per-token operator dependency graph (src/opentallas/critical_path.py) that replaced the flat per-layer floor (latency.*) and the two-all-reduces-per-layer link charge as the serial part of every decode step. The `latency` block is kept for the legacy floor, which every point still reports as a diagnostic.

rom_datapath.purpose: Measured depths of this repository's own hardwired decode datapath (rtl/hdc, rtl/hdc/v41). Every ROM-side operator node of the per-token dependency graph is priced from these; nothing here is fitted to any anchor.

clock_hz.note: The slowest routed fmax among the token path's units (ot_hdc_softplus, 1.034 GHz, closed; ot_hdc_matvec 1.067 GHz and ot_hdc_stream 1.111 GHz did not close at their probe targets), ASAP7 TT 0.7 V, applied unscaled to the N5/N6 designs.

matrix_engine_interleave.note: outputs in flight per matrix-engine lane; also sets the lane-walk floor of a small matvec

stream_depth_sigmoid_cycles.note: stream unit with the sigmoid SFU (K.su_depth[SFU_SIGM])

softplus_cycles.note: sqrt(softplus): exp, divide, Horner, sqrt; II 1

blockdot_cycles.note: FP8/FP4 block-scaled dot, last block to output

select_extra_cycles.note: a top-K select emits K+2 cycles after its last element in rank order, 2K+2 in ascending-index order

stream_lane_area_um2.note: area of one stream-unit element per cycle, SFU included, ASAP7, not scaled to N5/N6

stream_area_fraction.note: share of a die's compute area given to stream-unit lanes; the width is floor-power-of-two of that area over stream_lane_area_um2, at least 16

select_units_per_die.note: ot_hdc_select instances available to the first level of a top-k; the merge tree and ascending pass on merged input are not built RTL

hbm_random_row_latency_s.note: random-row HBM read latency, charged only where a gather address is data dependent (the rows an index scan selects); technology.json had no HBM latency constant

rom_row_access_s.note: one ROM row read for an embedding or Engram row gather

sinkhorn_unit_step_s.note: one whole 4x4 normalisation per unit clock; the unit runs as a multicycle path of the core clock, so a step costs ceil(step x core clock) core cycles. Same source as tools/decode_critical_path.py sinkhorn_unit().

sinkhorn_unit_clocks.note: unit clocks from accepting the exponentiated 4x4 to out_valid: 2 x iterations + 1. One user's Sinkhorn at a time: users in flight queue in rounds on one unit per sublayer engine.

gpu_datapath.purpose: The GPU side's serial per-token cost, priced on the same operator dependency graph as the ROM side: every dependent kernel pays a launch-and-synchronisation gap, every collective its measured small-message floor (links.*.hop_latency_s), and a dependent arithmetic chain inside one kernel its published instruction latencies. Graded, cited, never fitted.

kernel_launch_gap_s.source: Hazy Research, Look Ma, No Bubbles! Designing a Low-Latency Megakernel for Llama-1B (2025-05-27), https://hazyresearch.stanford.edu/blog/2025-05-27-no-bubbles ; NVIDIA Developer Blog, Getting Started with CUDA Graphs (A. Gray, 2019), https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/cuda-graphs/
kernel_launch_gap_s.note: Cost per dependent kernel boundary of a CUDA-graph decode step. STATED 1.3 us: measured on H100, "launch cost only decreases to around 1.3 microseconds" with CUDA graphs, against about 2.1 us with stream launches (the high end), and existing serving stacks issue "7 kernel launches per layer" for Llama-1B. LOW 0.5 us: V100, a 2.9 us kernel costs 3.4 us per kernel inside a CUDA graph (9.6 us with a per-kernel sync, 3.8 us with overlapped stream launches). Charged once per kernel on the graph's critical path, on both GPU parts; a megakernel that removes the boundaries is not a shipping serving stack and is not credited.

fp32_dependent_cycles.source: Jia, Maggioni, Staiger, Scarpazza, Dissecting the NVIDIA Volta GPU Architecture via Microbenchmarking, arXiv:1804.06826 (2018), section 4.1
fp32_dependent_cycles.note: "On Volta, most integer and single-precision instructions have a latency of 4 cycles" (6 on Pascal: the high end). Used for a dependent FP32 add or multiply inside one kernel.

fp32_divide_cycles.source: Jia et al. arXiv:1804.06826 (MUFU class 14 cycles on Pascal, 4-cycle FFMA on Volta); Abdelkhalik et al., Demystifying the Nvidia Ampere Architecture through Microbenchmarking, arXiv:2208.11174 Table V (div.rn.f32 and rcp.rn.f32 compile to a multi-instruction MUFU.RCP sequence)
fp32_divide_cycles.note: IEEE div.rn.f32 as compiled: MUFU.RCP (14) plus three dependent FFMA refinement steps (3 x 4) = 26 cycles on the dependent chain; the band spans an approximate reciprocal (18) to the slow-path fixup (40).

hardware_links.purpose: Links priced as hardware traversals with no software stack, on which the collective's logical algorithm (two-step, one-shot, ring, recursive doubling, tree, centre-rooted mesh; hierarchical across link classes) is searched per collective. Every other link's hop_latency_s is half a MEASURED small-message collective (see links.nvlink3), so a collective on it is priced as its measured floor per switch tier and no algorithm is credited beyond the measured best kernel.

rom_package_ucie.note: every die in a package has a direct link to every other; bytes_s is per link

rom_board_serdes.note: packages on a 2-D board mesh; bytes_s is per package, split over its 4 neighbour links

on_wafer.source: Rocki et al., Fast Stencil-Code Computation on a Wafer-Scale Processor, SC20, arXiv:2010.03660
on_wafer.note: reticle fields on the stitched wafer mesh; bytes_s is the whole wafer's, so one field edge carries bytes_s / fields per wafer / 4

on_wafer_n5.source: Cerebras (Sean Lie), Wafer-Scale AI: GPU Impossible Performance, Hot Chips 36, 2024, doi:10.1109/HCS61935.2024.10664673 ; Rocki et al., Fast Stencil-Code Computation on a Wafer-Scale Processor, SC20, arXiv:2010.03660

rom_wafer_serdes.note: wafers on direct neighbour SerDes; bytes_s is per wafer

rom_wafer_express.note: reticle fields on a dedicated express mesh; bytes_s is one field-edge link

determinism.two_step: fixed order: each shard is summed on its owner in rank order, then broadcast
determinism.one_shot: fixed order: every rank sums all partials in rank order (bit-identical replicas)
determinism.ring: fixed order per shard (ring order); deterministic run to run
determinism.rec_doubling: fixed pairing per step; IEEE add is commutative so all ranks hold the same bits
determinism.hierarchical: in-domain, then across domains, then an in-domain broadcast; each level fixed
determinism.measured_floor: the measured best small-message kernel (NVLink/InfiniBand); NCCL LL is deterministic for a fixed rank count

band.note: The per-layer serial cost is the dependent-operator chain of the Llama-3.1-8B decode graph priced with this repository's measured RTL depths (serial_latency.rom_datapath) -- nothing is fitted to this anchor -- and it is reported at both ends of the ranged inputs. 'per_layer_cost_that_would_close_the_gap_s' is what the chain would have to cost for the model to land exactly on the shipping rate; a value below the modelled chain means the model is SLOWER than the part, and the residual is the hardwired datapath's own serial depth, which the gate reports rather than tunes.
